+- Fixed ``catch()`` dropping exceptions that no handler matched when a handler raises
+  an exception. Such exceptions are now propagated along with the handler's
+  exception, like with native ``except*``, so code that previously received only the
+  handler's exception will now receive an exception group containing both
+  (`#161 <https://github.com/agronholm/exceptiongroup/issues/161>`_)

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("handler_error_type", [RuntimeError, KeyboardInterrupt])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("multiple_handlers", [False, True])
+def test_handler_raises_preserves_unmatched(handler_error_type, multiple_handlers):
+    handled = ValueError("handled")
+    unmatched = TypeError("unhandled")
+    handler_error = handler_error_type("handler failed")
+    original = BaseExceptionGroup("original", [handled, unmatched])
+    seen = []
+
+    def handler(group):
+        seen.append(group)
+        raise handler_error
+
+    handlers = {ValueError: handler}
+    if multiple_handlers:
+        handlers[LookupError] = lambda group: None
+
+    exceptions = ()
+    try:
+        with catch(handlers):
+            raise original
+    except BaseException as result:
+        assert isinstance(result, BaseExceptionGroup)
+        exceptions = result.exceptions
+
+    assert len(exceptions) == 2
+    assert exceptions[0] is handler_error
+    remainder = exceptions[1]
+    assert isinstance(remainder, ExceptionGroup)
+    assert remainder.message == "original"
+    assert remainder.exceptions == (unmatched,)
+    assert seen[0].exceptions == (handled,)
+    assert handler_error.__context__ is seen[0]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("reraise", [False, True], ids=["new_group", "bare_raise"])
+def test_handler_raises_group_preserves_unmatched(reraise):
+    unmatched = TypeError("unhandled")
+    new_group = ExceptionGroup("new", [RuntimeError("handler failed")])
+    seen = []
+
+    def handler(group):
+        seen.append(group)
+        if reraise:
+            raise
+        raise new_group
+
+    with pytest.raises(ExceptionGroup) as excgrp, catch({ValueError: handler}):
+        raise ExceptionGroup("original", [ValueError("handled"), unmatched])
+
+    assert len(excgrp.value.exceptions) == 2
+    assert excgrp.value.exceptions[0] is (seen[0] if reraise else new_group)
+    remainder = excgrp.value.exceptions[1]
+    assert remainder.message == "original"
+    assert remainder.exceptions == (unmatched,)
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "handler_error_type",
+    [
+        RuntimeError,
+        # PyPy's native except* raises an internal AssertionError when a handler
+        # raises KeyboardInterrupt, instead of propagating the new exception with
+        # the unmatched remainder of the group (works on CPython).
+        pytest.param(
+            KeyboardInterrupt,
+            marks=pytest.mark.skipif(
+                PYPY, reason="PyPy except* bug with KeyboardInterrupt"
+            ),
+        ),
+    ],
+)
+def test_handler_raises_preserves_unmatched_native(handler_error_type):
+    handled = ValueError("handled")
+    unmatched = TypeError("unhandled")
+    handler_error = handler_error_type("handler failed")
+    original = BaseExceptionGroup("original", [handled, unmatched])
+    exceptions = ()
+    try:
+        try:
+            raise original
+        except* ValueError:
+            raise handler_error
+    except BaseExceptionGroup as result:
+        exceptions = result.exceptions
+
+    assert len(exceptions) == 2
+    assert exceptions[0] is handler_error
+    assert exceptions[1].message == "original"
+    assert exceptions[1].exceptions == (unmatched,)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("reraise", [False, True], ids=["new_group", "bare_raise"])
+def test_handler_raises_group_preserves_unmatched(reraise):
+    unmatched = TypeError("unhandled")
+    new_group = ExceptionGroup("new", [RuntimeError("handler failed")])
+
+    # Like catch(), use a separate handler function: a bare "raise" directly in the
+    # except* block would merge the exceptions back into the original group instead
+    def handler(group):
+        if reraise:
+            raise
+        raise new_group
+
+    with pytest.raises(ExceptionGroup) as excgrp:
+        try:
+            raise ExceptionGroup("original", [ValueError("handled"), unmatched])
+        except* ValueError as eg:
+            matched = eg
+            handler(eg)
+
+    assert len(excgrp.value.exceptions) == 2
+    assert excgrp.value.exceptions[0] is (matched if reraise else new_group)
+    remainder = excgrp.value.exceptions[1]
+    assert remainder.message == "original"
+    assert remainder.exceptions == (unmatched,)
